history.summary: The headline 'cheap freehold' signal rests on a zero-transaction cohort and a size-class mismatch. Once compared to the right (2-BR-sized) comps, the discount mostly evaporates. Honest Neutral.
history.rating_rationale: psf_cohort_txns=0 means the -24.9% cohort premium has literally no same-size comparable behind it — exactly the v3.4 data-quirk pattern to be skeptical of. The 786 sqft unit is labelled 1-BR but is a 2-BR footprint, and the project's 2-BR median is ~$1,090 psf while only the tiny 398 sqft units fetch $1,400-$1,722 psf. So at $1,272 psf the unit is cheap versus small-unit prints but roughly fair-to-slightly-cheap versus its actual 2-BR-sized comps. Freehold is not a forward edge (v3.4). With the discount ambiguous, the developer being a budget builder, and the region (D15) only RCR-typical forward, there is no decisive edge — Neutral at low confidence is the honest call.
red_flags: psf_cohort_txns=0 — the cheapness signal has no same-size transaction support; classic thin-data quirk
Size-class mismatch: a 786 sqft '1-BR' is a 2-BR footprint; comparing it to 398 sqft small-unit PSF overstates the bargain
Fragrance Realty is a budget/mass developer with a mixed build-quality reputation

$999,999 asking is priced right at the psychological/ABSD-relevant ceiling, leaving little headroom
catalysts: Freehold tenure in the desirable D15 East Coast belt (downside floor, not a forward edge)
